grade.first_issue: The central claim that the accumulated prime sets P_n eventually stabilize is unsupported and actually false, so Rule E applies. For the admissible initial value a_1=2, the greedy rule gives a_n=2n; hence P_n eventually contains every prime p via a_p=2p and is unbounded.
grade.summary: The hitting-set formulation and the conditional argument that a stabilized finite prime universe would yield eventual periodicity are useful observations. However, the proposed proof of stabilization is only a probabilistic smooth-number heuristic and is contradicted by a basic valid sequence. Moreover, even the conditional argument proves the translation law only for n at least N; the assertion that determinism extends it backward to every positive n is unjustified, invoking the quantifier defect in Rule D. Proving the theorem requires a new structural idea, such as finiteness of the relevant minimal global hitting sets rather than finiteness of all primes occurring in the terms.
strengths: Correctly characterizes admissible next terms using minimal prime hitting sets and their squarefree products.
Correctly observes, conditionally, that stabilization of a finite admissibility pattern modulo a fixed modulus would make the later gaps periodic.

errors.description: The load-bearing assertion that P_n is bounded is false. With a_1=2 one obtains a_n=2n, whose terms introduce unboundedly many prime factors. The statements about the density of P_n-smooth numbers neither constitute a proof nor hold with the required bounded-gap strength.

The residue argument, even under its false stabilization hypothesis, establishes at most eventual translation-periodicity. Forward determinism does not imply that such a relation extends backward, so the required conclusion for every positive n remains unsupported.
